structured_output.summary: Independent review of Phase 22 chunk `typed-connections` (attempt 3/5) at reviewed source 78c4cd64…. The chunk delivers its declared milestones: a dedicated generated `red_team_management` model namespace (Vertex AI params, masked declaration-only twin, explicit `client_session` config with literal discriminator), two appended union tails verified positionally against `contracts/native-union-variants.json`, schema-bound enum vocabularies (`VERTEX_AI`/`N8N`/`REALTIME`) with frozen TypeScript-parity enums deliberately left intact and documented, four optional typed projections (`basic_username`/`basic_password`/`audio_request_json`/`audio_curl`) that preserve every formerly accepted raw value, derived profiling-filter vocabulary, regenerated graph/model/operation/export/qualification ledgers with a verified zero-live offline boundary, dual NOTICE attribution for pan.dev 582e3054/0.86.0, and a new packaged offline consumer example executed on both compilers. Generation is deterministic and fails closed on unreviewed vendor vocabulary, patterns, defaults, projection divergence, baseline node drift, model renames and union prefix changes, each with negative unit tests. Rust fixtures independently cover new/old/hybrid/unknown/missing-discriminator unions, both response modes, omission/null/value, redaction, pre-dispatch filter rejection and all five target operations end-to-end through a mock transport. Recorded check evidence is genuine, source-bound and complete for the documented 42-command Phase 22 gate; the generated-code correctness claim rests on green fmt/clippy(-D warnings)/test/doc/example runs on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 across the red-team and JSON-unification feature sets. Remaining issues are all low: the five-operation oracle compares against the same validator it exercises rather than a raw document, the new example has no content binding, the plan text still says to extend the frozen `TargetConnectionType`/`ResponseMode` enums, and `contracts/native-models.json` lists only the four baseline regex sources while the validator now implements seven. No blocker or high findings. Categories 9/9/9/9.5/9 = 45.5/50, above the 42 chunk floor and at the 45 aim.

findings.description: In `all_five_operations_preserve_declared_sensitive_response_shapes` the expected value for every one of the five operations is `validation::parse("TargetResponseSchema", expected, mode)` — the same validator the client path uses. A validator defect that dropped or rewrote a field would be invisible because both sides of the assertion would shift together. An independent raw-document anchor exists only in other tests (`vertex_client_session_and_new_values_preserve_both_response_modes:68`, `missing_defaults_and_explicit_null_are_distinct:167`), not per operation, so the plan's "every row requires both response modes, raw and typed round-trip fixtures" is only partially met per row.
findings.required_fix: In the `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults` iteration of the five-operation matrix, additionally assert `serde_json::to_value(actual).unwrap() == expected` against the hand-written response document so each of the five rows has a validator-independent raw round-trip oracle.

findings.description: `verify_runtime_adoption`'s required `sourceBindings` set and `management_runtime_evidence()` (line 679) omit `crates/scm-sdk/examples/red_team_management.rs`, the milestone 22.3 packaged consumer deliverable added in this attempt. Deleting it would be caught (the `cargo run` command in scripts/check-rust.py:71 would fail), but gutting its body to a trivial `main` would pass every gate. The repository already has a stronger precedent for binding example content (`tools/test_g10_release.py:100` verifies the response_defaults example's actual API usage).
findings.required_fix: Add `crates/scm-sdk/examples/red_team_management.rs` to the overlay `sourceBindings`/`management_runtime_evidence` path list, or assert its required API usage (Vertex builder, `Variant3` client session, `TargetCreateRequestResponseMode::REALTIME`, both response modes, `profiling_status`) the way `verify_rust_additions` does for the G10 example.

findings.description: The plan still instructs "Extend `TargetConnectionType` with `VERTEX_AI`, `N8N`; extend `ResponseMode` with `REALTIME`". The implementation instead keeps those frozen TypeScript-parity enums unchanged (generated.rs:174153, 162443 — `VERTEX_AI` and `REALTIME` resolve to `Unknown(String)`, asserted at crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_management_models.rs:158) and names the new values on `TargetCreateRequestConnectionType`/`TargetCreateRequestResponseMode`. The decision is sound (those parity enums are not referenced by any model field, so there is no wire effect) and is recorded in the overlay ledger's `enumCompatibility` plus generated rustdoc, but the authoritative plan text and docs/PHASES.md were not reconciled, leaving a reader with contradictory guidance about which public enum carries the new variants.
findings.required_fix: Update the plan's connection/union section (and the Phase 24 changelog obligation) to state the frozen-parity versus schema-bound enum split explicitly, naming `TargetCreateRequestConnectionType`/`TargetCreateRequestResponseMode` as the types that declare `VERTEX_AI`, `N8N` and `REALTIME`.

findings.description: `structuralChecks.regexSources` records only the four frozen baseline patterns, while `crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1058-1066` now implements seven (the three reviewed Vertex request patterns were added) and tools/generate_models.py:897 enforces the union. The new patterns are traceable through tools/red_team_management_models.py:21, the committed schema graph and the vendor compatibility-decisions ledger, but the model contract ledger itself now understates the implemented request-validation surface.
findings.required_fix: Either extend `structuralChecks` with an explicitly labelled overlay-owned regex list (e.g. `managementRegexSources`) derived from `red_team_management_models.PATTERNS`, or add a one-line note in the ledger/docs stating that overlay-owned request patterns are recorded in contracts/red-team-management-model-overlay.json and the vendor compatibility decisions rather than here.
